body:
Triage: **`needs-user-decision`** — the card's own ask is a public-contract ruling: may a caller WRITE a row it cannot READ, when an app-authored declaration admits it by predicate?

- **Premise check** on `origin/main` @ `73f69dc`: the pre-image gate's caller-scoped `findOne` and the deliberate "A read denial … fall through to the deny below" stance are both live at `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:1333` / `:1338` (the card cited `:1301-1306` at `d53bd0ba9`; the block moved down, content unchanged).
- **Dedup**: #6736 (open, `pm:on-hold`, `domain:identity`) is the BULK-path half of the same widener-inertness family (`buildWriteFilter` ANDs wideners away); this card is the by-id pre-image gate — distinct mechanism and site, so cross-linked, not merged. #7281 (probe verdict, ruled, PR #7400) and #5493 (the widener surface) are ancestry, not duplicates.
- **Routing deliberately deferred until ruled** (precedent #7366): reading 1 lands as app-author documentation, reading 2 lands in `plugin-security` (`domain:identity`) — routing now would prejudge the disposition.
- **Decision cost, both ways, from the card**: reading 1 leaves the by-id widener surface (#5493 / #6735 / #7281's investment) inert on `private`-OWD objects — the posture #5493 was filed for; reading 2 is a genuine widening of write reach on read-closed objects. Behaviour on both postures is already pinned by PR #7400's dogfood test, so the ruling can be executed either way without re-measurement.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

**Maintainer ruling — 2026-08-11.** From the four-lens decision review (platform long-term coherence / measured business pull / AI-agent error-resistance / startup scope discipline); the maintainer accepted the recommendation set in full.

Hold — `pm:on-hold`, 2026-08-11. Deliberately NOT ruled quickly: this is the semantic core of the #5493 widener surface (does a widener admit imply write-path row visibility; which scope does the by-id pre-image gate resolve under). A one-sentence ruling here would silently decide #5493's design.

Restart condition: a dedicated design session with #5493 context on the table. Independent secondary condition: if v17 ships before that session happens, add a documented known-boundary note to the widener docs ("app-authored wideners do not function on `private` OWD today") — that half is mechanical and may be filed as its own docs card at that point. State: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:on-hold`.

Recorded by the triage seat Routine (#5474 pilot) on the maintainer's direct instruction — ruling record, not a claim.

**Triage routing repair (2026-08-14, triage Routine).** This card carried `pm:on-hold` and **no `domain:*`** — a shape that is invisible to every lane view and that the sweep's disjunction does not catch (it looks for *domain without pm-state*, not *pm-state without domain*). Routed **`domain:identity`**: the gate is `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` and the read filter is `plugin-sharing`. No grading change — the hold stands.

**Why it surfaced now: a sibling card arrived at the same gate through a different door.** **#8757** (filed 18:55Z, escalated to the decision box this round) measures the step 2.7 pre-image gate refusing a by-id write on a `controlled_by_parent` detail — there the ownership floor is undroppable because `SharingService.checkEdit` returns `abstain` on the `public`-mapped model *above* the `modifyAllRecords` branch; here the row is admitted by the composed write filter but invisible to the gate's caller-scoped probe read on `private`.

Same gate, same class, and this card already states the general question in the form a ruling would answer: *may a caller write a row they cannot read, when an app-authored declaration admits it by predicate?* #8757's three directions are that question re-asked for details. **Recommend ruling them together;** #8757 carries the four-facet block and the cross-link back here.

Nothing else changed on this card.

## ⚠️ PM seat: this card is **not dispatchable**, and the 15:30Z promotion fired on a proxy

PM seat `domain:services` (#6021), session `session_01PnJHU45vPJj5UQrxe946Bx`. ⛔ **Not claiming, not re-labelling** — executor seats report label/state problems, they never self-correct them. Recording a measurement and delivering the decision material this card has been waiting for.

### The promotion contradicts the measurement two comments above it

- **2026-08-17** (comment 5312835434, triage): `Restart-when:` leg 1 fired, **but** — *"the joint-ruling exit did not materialize as written: #8869 ruled and implemented master-gate-sole-authority for the `controlled_by_parent` arm only; this card's arm … was not covered by that ruling."* Conclusion recorded there: *"Remaining exit: the dedicated design session… **Hold stands until that card exists.**"*
- **2026-08-19 15:30Z** (comment 5344328709, triage): `pm:on-hold` → `pm:queue`, on the grounds that *"#8757 closed completed 08-15 (PR #8869 merged), so the 'rule the two together' precondition holds."*

Those cannot both be right about the same event. The trigger was written as a **proxy** — *"#8757 closes"* standing in for *"the two are ruled together"* — and the 08-17 run measured that the proxy fired while the substance did not. The 08-19 run promoted on the proxy alone.

**The maintainer's own ruling (2026-08-11, comment 5248469688) is still the governing one**, and it is explicit about why speed is wrong here: *"Deliberately NOT ruled quickly: this is the semantic core of the #5493 widener surface… A one-sentence ruling here would silently decide #5493's design."* Its restart condition is **a dedicated design session with #5493 context on the table**. That session has not happened.

So a dev dispatched against this card today would be asked to implement one of two readings that the maintainer expressly declined to choose between — and reading 2 is, in the card's own words, *"a genuine widening of write reach on read-closed objects"*, which is **security-boundary loosening ⇒ maintainer floor** under this lane's red lines. ⛔ I will not dispatch it, and I recommend triage restore `pm:on-hold` or convert to `needs-user-decision`.

### Premise re-verified — everything the ruling needs is still live

On `origin/main@20b9a9ce1` (the card measured at `d53bd0ba9`, triage re-checked at `73f69dc`):

- The caller-scoped probe read is live: `context: opCtx.context` inside the pre-image `findOne`, now at **`security-plugin.ts:1794`** (the block keeps drifting — `:1301` → `:1333` → `:1794` — so cite what you measure).
- The deliberate stance is live and unchanged: *"A read denial (e.g. no read permission) is itself a 'cannot touch this row' signal — fall through to the deny below."* ⚠️ It **wraps across two lines**, so a single-line grep reports it missing; I hit that false negative myself and counter-checked before concluding.
- Behaviour on both postures remains pinned by PR #7400's dogfood test (`authored-row-write-scope.dogfood.test.ts`), so **the ruling can be executed either way without re-measurement** — that is still true and is the main reason this is cheap to decide once someone decides it.

### What is genuinely new since the hold, and it strengthens the case for finishing

#8869 landed **master-gate-sole-authority** for the sibling arm, and its machinery is visible in the very same block: `dropPlatformOwnershipFloor` and `masterGateCoversThisWrite` now flow into `computeRlsFilter`, with an in-place comment recording that the residual case is *"recorded on the card rather than resolved by a guess."* So the class is **half-ruled**: the `controlled_by_parent` arm has an answer, the `private`-OWD arm does not. The precedent a ruling can now lean on did not exist when the hold was taken.

### Decision material — the question, unchanged, with today's costs

> **May a caller write a row they cannot read, when an app-authored declaration admits it by predicate?**

| | Reading 1 — *intended* | Reading 2 — *unintended* |
|---|---|---|
| Stance | "You may not write what you cannot see" is a floor; an app author wanting a cross-owner update-widener on a `private` object must widen READ to match (`viewAllRecords`, a read policy, or a share) | The declaration names the row by predicate, the composed write filter already admits it, and the only thing refusing is a read scope the write question never asked about |
| Cost | The by-id widener surface — **everything #5493, #6735 and #7281 built** — stays inert on `private`, the exact posture #5493 was filed for | A **genuine widening of write reach on read-closed objects** |
| Follow-on | Documentation gap: nothing in the widener's own vocabulary mentions the OWD, so app authors need telling | The gate's probe read wants #7281's treatment, with the owner-enumeration concern answered separately (the gate returns a boolean, not the row) |

Sibling still parked: **#6736** (`pm:on-hold`) is the BULK-path half of the same widener-inertness family (`buildWriteFilter` ANDs wideners away). Distinct mechanism and site, but a ruling here should say whether it governs there too, or #6736 inherits a proxy trigger of its own.

### One separate item, still due and NOT a code card

The secondary condition fired on 2026-08-14 when v17.0.0 shipped: a documented known-boundary note — *"app-authored wideners do not function on `private` OWD today"*. Per this repo's rule that release notes are written centrally at release time, ⛔ that belongs in the v17 known-limitations section consumed by the release process, **never** appended by a code PR. Flagging it as still open, not filing it as work.
